best_for: Developers who already live in tmux or a tiling window manager and want a fast terminal they configure in one text file.

points.title: Fast because it is small
points.text: Alacritty draws with OpenGL and leaves extra features to other tools. The project says working with other programs, rather than copying them, is how it stays fast.

points.title: No tabs, no splits
points.text: By design it has no tabs or split panes. You use tmux or your window manager for that, and there is no settings window either.

points.title: Configured in TOML
points.text: Everything lives in `alacritty.toml`, which you create yourself; on Windows it goes in `%APPDATA%\alacritty\`. Version 0.17.0 added TOML 1.1 syntax and mouse wheel bindings.

points.title: Called beta by its makers
points.text: The README still calls Alacritty beta, with some missing features and bugs, though many people use it daily. It is free under the Apache 2.0 license.

points.title: Windows needs 1809 or later
points.text: The Windows build needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later for ConPTY, and a GPU with at least OpenGL ES 2.0. The MSI is x64 and installs for the whole machine.

points.title: A catch on the Mac
points.text: The Mac download is a universal disk image. Homebrew disabled its Alacritty cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails macOS Gatekeeper checks, so expect a security prompt when you first open it.

points.title: Linux comes from your distro
points.text: Linux and BSD users install it through their package manager; this site lists only Windows and Mac. The Windows listing keeps 19 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
